question: How does one guṇa increase over the others?
premises: Overcoming rajas and tamas, sattva becomes dominant, O Bharata.
Rajas overcomes sattva and tamas; tamas overcomes sattva and rajas.
Overcoming rajas and tamas, sattva increases.
Rajas overcomes sattva and tamas; tamas overcomes sattva and rajas.
inference: A guṇa increases when it overcomes the other two guṇas; the increase of guṇas arises through their mutual overcoming.
uncertainties: The supplied gloss leaves elliptical subjects in some clauses; the parallel structure supplies them.
This rendering follows the supplied Kashmirian-edition tokens and does not harmonize to the vulgate.
plain_english: O Bharata, when rajas and tamas are overcome, sattva becomes dominant; rajas overcomes sattva and tamas, and tamas overcomes sattva and rajas. Thus, when rajas and tamas are overcome, sattva increases; rajas overcomes sattva and tamas, and tamas overcomes sattva and rajas. It is said that the increase of a guṇa comes by mutual overcoming.
